newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - EBRD's the one with won.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - EBRD's the one with won.

text.p: The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development launched its South Korean won-denominated deal during late Asian hours on Monday.
The 94.8 billion Korean won bond has a 23.7 billion won offshore tranche, which is lead managed by Merrill Lynch International, acting as bookrunner, and by KDB Securities.
The offshore issue has 10 percent coupon payable semi-annualy and was priced and re-offered at 100.25 to yield 9.935 percent semi-annually or 10.182 percent annually.
At 10.182 percent, the AAA-rated EBRD bond is paying a higher annual yield than the World Bank's issue launched last Friday, which paid 10.04 percent on an annual basis.
The World Bank and now the EBRD are the first issuers to launch won-denominated Eurobonds.
Fees are higher for the EBRD issue at 40 basis points versus 25 basis points for the World Bank deal.
In other news, the Philippine Central Bank said today that it would launch its debut Yankee bond issue on April 15.
The central bank hopes to sell US$1.0 billion worth of bonds in 30- and 100-year tranches.
Bankers have speculated that the Philippines would forego the century bond because of the interest rate environment in the United States.
Many analysts foresee further increases in U.S. interest rates after the Federal Reserve raised the federal funds rate last month by 25 basis points to 5.50 percent.
Last week, Thailand opted to scupper its 30-year bond and stick with a 10-year issue, partly because of concerns about rising interest rates,
The Philippines central bank said it was going ahead with the issue despite criticism in congress that the issue would result in an increase in the country's foreign debt and interest payments.

"The actual debt servicing cost is likely to be very small or even negative. The central bank will be re-investing the bond proceeds in safe and liquid earning assets that will generate interest and other income that will mostly offset the interest expense on the Yankee bond or even generate some net income," the central bank said.
In Hong Kong, more banks are in the market for local currency floating rate certificate of deposit financing.

Wing Hang Bank and Bank of East Asia have mandated banks to arrange FRCD issues. Both are expected to be eligible for use at the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's Liquidity Adjustment Facility (LAF), or discount window.
Union Bank of Hong Kong also will raise funds via Hong Kong dollar FRCDs.
